title: Results Section Audit
subject: evidence-scoped audit of a synthetic optimizer-results excerpt
summary: The excerpt contains a universal optimality and timing claim that is contradicted by the reported solver logs, followed by an unsupported real-time deployment conclusion. The supplied evidence supports only a bounded description of the 12 solver runs.
footer: Generated from the canonical text audit. The HTML is a presentation of that audit and adds no scientific finding, number, correction, or conclusion.

findings.title: Global-optimum guarantee is contradicted by the solver logs
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s.
findings.evidence: The excerpt reports that only 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL. The other 3 reached the 60 s time limit with feasible incumbents and final relative gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%.
findings.consequence: The universal claim of global optimality within 10 s is false for the supplied evaluation set and is also inconsistent with the reported 60 s time limit and nonzero final gaps.
findings.correction: Replace the sentence with a bounded report of the logs: 9 of 12 runs ended with solver status OPTIMAL under the stated 1% relative MIP-gap tolerance, while 3 reached the 60 s limit with feasible incumbents and final gaps of 4.1%, 5.3%, and 7.8%. Do not call the latter runs globally optimal without an exact-optimality certificate.

findings.title: Real-time deployment readiness is unsupported
findings.source: The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: No deployment experiment, exact-optimality certificate, or timing measurements outside the solver logs are supplied. The logs include three time-limited runs with final gaps up to 7.8%.
findings.consequence: The conclusion extends bounded solver-log observations to operational readiness without evidence for deployment behavior, timing compliance, or exact solution quality.
findings.correction: Remove the deployment-readiness conclusion. Restrict the result to the observed 12 solver runs and state that deployment readiness was not evaluated.

findings.title: The reported timing does not support a 10-second claim
findings.source: The optimizer always returns the global optimum within 10 s. ... The method is therefore ready for real-time deployment.
findings.evidence: The supplied timing evidence consists only of solver logs reporting a 60 s time limit; no per-run wall-clock measurements or deployment timing measurements are provided.
findings.consequence: A reader cannot verify the 10 s threshold or infer real-time deadline compliance from the reported logs.
findings.correction: Provide per-run timing measurements and the deployment deadline and protocol before making a timing or real-time claim. If those artifacts remain unavailable, omit the 10 s and deployment statements and report only the stated solver-limit outcomes.
